position: Current Regulations That Should Be Rolled Back (Equity in IDEA)
proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Department begin rulemaking at once to rescind the Equity in IDEA (significant disproportionality) regulation, which requires states to consider race and ethnicity in identifying, placing and disciplining students with disabilities, with no replacement regulation. It also recommends that OSERS prepare a digest of research on the subject and send it to state superintendents and special education leaders to discourage states from continuing the practice.

status_summary: No proposed or final rule rescinding the 2016 Equity in IDEA regulation has been published as of 2026-10-12. ED published a notice on 2025-08-22 proposing to remove the significant disproportionality data collection from the IDEA Part B annual state application to reduce burden, and submitted the revised application to OMB with a notice on 2026-01-09. The Unified Agenda entry RIN 1820-AB84 lists an Equity in IDEA rule at the proposed rule stage, to amend the 2016 regulation including the standard methodology, with a proposed rule targeted for August 2026; K-12 Dive reported on 2026-07-07 that the changes had not been disclosed. The stage is proposed and the match partial, because the agenda describes an amendment rather than a rescission with no replacement, and no research digest sent to states was found.

timeline.event: ED published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice proposing to remove the significant disproportionality data collection under 34 CFR 300.646 and 300.647 from the IDEA Part B annual state application, citing burden reduction; comments were due 2025-10-21.
ED published a notice submitting the revised Part B annual state application to OMB; per the Federal Register abstract, the revision removes the significant disproportionality data collection.
K-12 Dive reported that the 2026 Unified Agenda planned an Equity in IDEA proposed rule for August 2026 to amend the regulation and that ED had not disclosed the changes.
The Federal Register published the introduction to the 2026 Unified Agenda, which matches a search for the Equity in IDEA item.

title: Rescind the 2016 Equity in IDEA rule with no replacement and send states a research digest
uncertainties: The Unified Agenda entry page gives a timetable of August 2026 but no publication date of its own; its source date is the date K-12 Dive reported the entry. The Federal Register introduction to the 2026 agenda was matched by a search for the item but its text was not read in this review. A Federal Register API search for Equity in IDEA and for significant disproportionality from 2025-01-20 found only the two information-collection notices and the agenda introduction, and no proposed rule. Whether OMB approved the revised Part B application was not confirmed. The 2018 delay rule and the 2019 court ruling vacating it were not re-verified and are background only. No evidence either way was found on an OSERS research digest.
